newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: GUATEMALA 97-98 COFFEE EXPORTS SEEN 3.2 MLN BAGS.
newsitem.headline: GUATEMALA 97-98 COFFEE EXPORTS SEEN 3.2 MLN BAGS.

text.p: Guatemalan coffee exports for the 1997/1998 harvest are predicted to be 3.2 million 60- kilo bags of washed arabicas, the National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said on Monday.
"That does not count unwashed, stock lots or robustas," Anacafe President Julio Arrivillaga told Reuters.
Coffee exports for the current year, which ends in September, are at 4.02 million 60-kilo bags as of Aug. 7, including all types of beans.

Even taking into account other types of beans, Arrivillaga said the next harvest will probably be a little lower than the one that is finishing now because every other coffee year is lower, and because the "El Nino" weather phenomenon could affect production.
Arrivillaga said original estimates for the current harvest were low because ANACAFE did not know about some new coffee farms that harvested for the first time.

"There were small producers this year that we hadn't taken into account," Arrivillaga said. Most of the new producers are in the western highlands of Huehuetenango and on the southwestern coastal areas, he added.
Arrivillaga said contraband coffee from neighboring countries was not the reason exports were higher than expected this year.
Black market coffee from neighboring El Salvador and Honduras has in the past been traded via Guatemala.
